children: She previously led marketing for Nothing in India

DailyObjects, the Indian-born design-led lifestyle tech brand, has appointed Zeenah Vilcassim as its Global Chief Marketing Officer. With over 17 years of experience across the US, Europe, the Middle East, China and India, she brings deep expertise in building brands, growing consumer businesses and taking propositions into new markets.
In her new role, Vilcassim will lead DailyObjects’ global brand and marketing strategy as the company builds on its success in India and advances its international ambitions.

Before joining DailyObjects, she led marketing for Nothing in India. She previously served as CEO of Zomato Live, now District by Zomato, where she built the business from the ground up. Earlier, as chief marketing officer at Bacardi India, she led consumer and customer marketing across the company’s portfolio. She also served as global brand director for Whiskies at Bacardi, shaping brand strategy across international markets.

Commenting on the appointment, Pankaj Garg, co-founder and CEO, DailyObjects, says, “DailyObjects is at an important point in its journey. As we build for the next phase of growth, we wanted a leader who combines an instinctive understanding of consumers with the ability to build distinctive brands across markets. Zeenah’s experience spans global brand stewardship, high-growth consumer businesses and building new ventures from the ground up, capabilities that closely reflect the demands of this role. Her ambition for the brand is aligned with ours, and we are delighted to have her lead DailyObjects’ global brand and marketing journey.”

Vilcassim adds, “What stands out about DailyObjects is that it has already built the foundations of a truly distinctive lifestyle brand: a clear point of view on design, a strong understanding of contemporary consumers and the capability to create products that belong in people’s everyday lives. Pankaj and Saurav’s ambition to take an India-born brand to the world strongly resonates with my own belief that the next generation of global consumer brands can be built with both local relevance and international appeal. I look forward to bringing together consumer insight, brand-building rigour and market-specific storytelling to help make DailyObjects a brand that is meaningful to consumers wherever it goes.”
She began her career as an economist and management consultant at Ernst & Young before moving into consumer and brand marketing.
The appointment comes as DailyObjects builds on its India-born design proposition and expands its reach to a wider global audience.
